_note: The Flight Director's words. Rules in src/ai/flightDirector.ts choose which ones to use, so the text can be rewritten here without touching any code.

outcome.orbit: You got there. The spacecraft is in orbit around {target} and the science is coming home.
outcome.flyby: The spacecraft reached {target} but could not stop, so it carried on past. Everything else about the mission worked.
outcome.lost: We lost the spacecraft on the way. That happens to real missions too, and the design was not the only reason.

praise.threeStars: This is how a mission is supposed to go: it arrived, it did nearly all the science it set out to do, and it came in under budget.
praise.cheap: You brought it in with ${moneyLeft}M to spare. That is the Mangalyaan lesson — a cheap mission that works beats an expensive one that nearly does.
praise.fullScience: Almost all the science got home, which means the antenna was the right size for the distance.
praise.survived: It survived everything the trip threw at it, which is worth as much as the science.

tips.antenna: Only {sciencePercent}% of your science reached Earth. At {target} the small antenna is a bottleneck — the large dish sends ten times as much, and it only costs $10M more.
tips.power: Power was tight at {target}, where sunlight is {sunlightPercent}% of what it is at Earth. Bigger panels, or a nuclear battery, would give the instruments room to breathe.
tips.fuel: You arrived with {fuelLeft} kg of fuel. That is a thin margin — one more course correction and there would have been nothing left for the braking burn.
tips.noFuel: There was not enough fuel for the braking burn. Next time load more, or fly a bigger rocket so the spacecraft has less work to do.
tips.risk: You took {riskPercent}% risk into the arrival. Every ignored problem adds to that number, and it is all cashed in at once on the last day.
tips.instruments: You carried {instrumentCount} instrument{plural}. There was room and money for more, and more instruments means more science.
tips.budgetTight: You spent almost all of the money. Money left over is worth points on its own, so a cheaper part is sometimes the better part.
tips.safeChoices: You took the safe option every time, which is why it arrived. Just remember the green opportunity cards are usually worth the risk.

signOff.good: Good flying. Try a harder mission.
signOff.mixed: A solid mission. Change one thing and fly it again.
signOff.bad: Have another go — you know what went wrong now, and that is most of the job.
